algorithm: Verify packet bounds before reading fields. Deny source addresses before rate accounting. Track per-source windows and count every action. XDP returns PASS or DROP at ingress. Reference: https://docs.kernel.org/bpf/ and https://github.com/libbpf/libbpf .
architecture: Reference: Ethernet bytes → IPv4 parser → policy → counters. Native: XDP hook → map policy → verdict; tracepoint → ring buffer. User-space control supplies explicit planned commands.
data_model: IPv4 addresses are network-order four-byte map keys. Deny values are one byte. Native counters: 0 pass, 1 deny, 2 rate, 3 malformed. Trace events carry attempted target UID and current UID.
description: A packet-policy reference with original XDP filtering and setuid tracepoint source plus a deliberate dry-run deployment workflow.
design: Loading code into a kernel changes networking behavior, so the loader prints a plan by default and only attaches with explicit --apply. It never selects an interface or assumes privileges automatically.
family_notes: Pass valid packets from distinct permitted sources.
Drop every packet from a denied source.
Rate-limit a single source beyond eight packets per window.
limitations: No BPF compiler, libbpf headers, bpftool or privileged kernel attachment was available. Kernel programs are uncompiled/unverified sources. Python policy is global per source; native rate buckets are per CPU, so multi-CPU aggregate limits differ. Setuid tracing observes attempts, not successful unauthorized privilege escalation. VLAN, IPv6 and checksum enforcement are not implemented; non-IPv4 traffic passes.
operations: Use a disposable Linux VM or dedicated test interface. Compile against that kernel and libbpf. Inspect verifier logs; stage traffic replay before explicit attachment. Keep an out-of-band way to detach XDP.
scope: Python binary packet builder/parser, deny/rate policy and exact counters. Native C XDP bounds checks, deny map, per-CPU LRU rate buckets, action counters and setuid-attempt ring-buffer tracepoint. Control helpers produce argument-safe bpftool/ip plans.
security: Kernel sources are unexecuted. Attaching XDP can drop network traffic. The loader defaults to printing a plan; use only an explicitly selected test interface and review verifier output first.
title: eBPF Network Observability & Security Agent
